newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian industry prices fall in first nine months.
newsitem.headline: Algerian industry prices fall in first nine months.

text.p: Algeria's non-oil and gas industry gate prices rose 19 percent in the first three quarters of 1996, compared with a 33.7 percent increase in the same period last year, official data showed on Wednesday.
The government's National Office of Statistics said the gate prices decline was prompted by free-market oriented reforms and an exchange currency rate stabilisation.
The gate prices rate in the non-oil state-owned industry rose 2.1 percent in the third quarter of 1996 from the second quarter.
Prices in private industry fell 0.3 percent in the third quarter this year in comparison with the second quarter, according to the data carried on the official Algerian news agency APS.
The National Office of Statistics said that, compared with respective quarters in 1995, industry gate prices showed a slower rate of increase over 1996.
They rose 12.5 percent in the third quarter of 1996 against the same period 1995, 19.1 percent in the second quarter of this year and 26.3 percent in the first three months of 1996.
The sharpest increase was in the electricity sector where the prices increased by 37.3 percent in the first three quarters of 1996 compared to the same period last year.

The government, striving to shift the once centrally commanded economy towards an open market, was focusing efforts this year to improve non-energy industrial production which fell by 7.4 percent in the first half of 1996 compared to the same period in 1995.

Algeria's state-owned non-oil and gas industry, experiencing difficulties after three decades of socialist operation, suffered most of a Moslem guerrillas sabotage campaign in the past three years with damage estimated at $2.0 billion.

The government has been locked in a five-year-old conflict with Moslem guerrillas since the cancellation of a general election in 1992 which radical Islamists were poised to win. About 60,000 people have died in the strife.
